candidate.accessibility_delta: If successful, local/GB10 inference becomes faster per watt and more useful for home research infrastructure without requiring larger hosted models.
candidate.baseline_to_beat: Published/static speculative-decoding schedule or local backend default measured by accepted tokens per cycle, end-to-end decode tok/s, and p50/p95 latency at concurrency 1/N.
candidate.description: Review DeepSpec/DSpark source material and run the smallest credible local or GB10 baseline to measure where speculative decoding time is actually spent before changing scheduler policy.
candidate.hypothesis: Adaptive online verification scheduling for DSpark-style speculative decoding can beat static SPS(B)-style draft/verify curves on Enoch agentic workloads while preserving output correctness.
candidate.implementation: Inspect DeepSpec paper/code, choose a small supported Qwen/Gemma or equivalent local model path, record baseline acceptance and latency curves, then test one adaptive scheduler policy against the static baseline.
candidate.kill_condition: Stop escalation if the smallest supported model path cannot run reproducibly, if acceptance improvements do not translate to wall-clock throughput, or if GB10 bottlenecks are dominated by unrelated backend limitations.
likely_failure_modes: DeepSpec dependencies or cache footprint too large
scheduler overhead erases acceptance gains
GB10 bottleneck is KV/cache movement rather than drafter math
agentic prompts have poor acceptance profiles
candidate.mechanism: Track recent acceptance-by-position, entropy/prompt class, backend load, and KV/cache pressure, then choose draft lengths and verification budget dynamically instead of using one static schedule.
candidate.novelty_comparison: Distinct from generic speculative decoding because the proposed unit is scheduler adaptation on Enoch/GB10 agentic workload traces with wall-clock falsification.

candidate.accessibility_delta: Improves local-model usefulness by finding post-training recipes that extract more capability per parameter/update instead of requiring larger hosted models.
candidate.baseline_to_beat: Naive small-data SFT or few-shot/no-finetune baseline under the same model, data volume, and evaluation harness.
candidate.description: Turn the post-training/fine-tuning research idea into a bounded empirical matrix rather than a literature-only survey.
candidate.hypothesis: Small, controlled post-training experiments can reveal capability-per-update gains from data difficulty, trace quality, selective updates, ordering, and replay that broad SFT/RL comparisons hide.
candidate.implementation: Build a literature matrix, choose one low-cost base model and target capability suite, define leakage-controlled train/eval manifests, and run or dry-run a tiny baseline once the dataset-quality scorer has a v0 fixture.
candidate.kill_condition: Stop if data provenance/leakage cannot be controlled, if training cost exceeds the bounded local budget, or if metrics cannot distinguish in-domain memorization from transfer.
likely_failure_modes: dataset leakage masks real transfer
tiny run too underpowered
training stack cost exceeds local budget
method axis confounded by dataset quality
candidate.mechanism: Hold model and compute budget fixed while varying dataset selection, difficulty bands, diversity score, LoRA target modules, and replay/regularization, then compare in-domain and OOD transfer.
candidate.novelty_comparison: Distinct from generic fine-tuning exploration because the metric is capability per update under controlled data-quality and OOD transfer axes.

candidate.accessibility_delta: Helps local researchers train smaller models more efficiently by selecting higher-signal data instead of chasing raw data scale.
candidate.baseline_to_beat: Size-only, random-slice, or simple cleanliness/dedup heuristics for choosing training data.
candidate.description: Prototype a dataset-quality scorer that measures generalized learning signal rather than only corpus size or superficial cleanliness.
candidate.hypothesis: Dataset diversity, concept coverage, compositional richness, difficulty balance, and transfer proxy scores can predict when a smaller model can approach a larger model with better data.
candidate.implementation: Define a v0 metric schema, run it on two or more contrasting fixture datasets, generate per-axis reports, then correlate at least one score with a tiny downstream fine-tune/eval or proxy evaluation.
candidate.kill_condition: Stop or redesign if the metrics are dominated by noise, can be gamed by diverse-but-wrong text, or do not correlate with any downstream/proxy outcome on fixture slices.
likely_failure_modes: semantic diversity rewards noise
embedding/gradient proxies too expensive
fixture datasets too small to correlate
anti-gaming checks under-specified
candidate.mechanism: Score datasets before training across lexical entropy, semantic cluster richness, concept/relation graph density, compositional held-out coverage, gradient-space diversity, difficulty bands, redundancy, and downstream transfer proxy.
candidate.novelty_comparison: Distinct from model-output benchmarks because it scores training data learnability before training and checks against transfer outcomes.
